name: Element.makeelement
note: review: CopyIndependentPy only says the original's attributes are unchanged after setting one on the copy, so a makeelement that returns an element with no attributes satisfies it; that the copy has the original's attributes is not stated.

name: Element.__copy__
note: review: copyPy omits elem.text/elem.tail and elem[:] = self (:191-193, which iterates self through __getitem__ and type-checks each child), and the property passes for a copy that loses its attributes.

name: Element.__setitem__
note: review: setSlicePy mirrors the type-check loop then the list store, but SetSliceTwinsSeq assumes every item is an Element and the excluded case is not on record: the twin raises TypeError before list's extended-slice size check while C checks the size first (e[::2] = [5] on four children: TypeError here, ValueError in C); indices are Int, so a non-int, non-slice key reaches no theorem.

name: Element.extend
note: review: extendPy runs an iterator's effects only at the first __next__, but this loop appends while it iterates, so effects between items are not expressible: e.extend(e) never ends in the twin (Element has no __iter__, so the __getitem__ iteration sees each append) while C snapshots with PySequence_Fast and doubles the children, a difference not on record.

name: Element.insert
note: review: WritersTwins assumes T.isElem x, so the _assert_is_element TypeError in this body (:245) is never exercised, and an insert without the check still satisfies it.

name: Element.remove
note: review: The citation 'ElementTree.py:247-270' in EtreeRemove.lean points at _assert_is_element and part of remove, but 3.15.2's remove is :254-274; the model itself (list.remove, then the ValueError conversion) matches the body.
